exposure: Laparoscopic lateral suspension (LLS) surgery for pelvic organ prolapse (POP)
outcome: Pregnancy outcomes (spontaneous abortion, premature delivery, normal pregnancy progression)
cohort: The study included 11 women of reproductive age who became pregnant after undergoing uterus-sparing laparoscopic lateral suspension (LLS) surgery for pelvic organ prolapse (POP) stage II-III.
finding: Laparoscopic lateral suspension (LLS) appears to be a safe and effective uterus-preserving procedure for women with pelvic organ prolapse who desire future fertility, with pregnancies progressing normally and low recurrence rates.
mod_finding: All deliveries were conducted via cesarean section, which may be the preferred delivery mode to minimize the risk of prolapse recurrence.
followup_time: 3-6 months and up to 2-5 years after LLS; delivery outcomes were observed during the pregnancy.
birth_weight: All babies, except two premature deliveries, exhibited a weight commensurate with their gestational age.
gest_age: All babies, except two premature deliveries, exhibited a weight commensurate with their gestational age.
